_provenance.what: Dated Indian eclipse records and Parameśvara's fitted epoch, as quoted in Nīlakaṇṭha Somayājī's Jyotirmīmāṃsā. These are the engine's class-(ii) referees: historical observations recorded in Indian sources. No ephemeris was used to produce or check any entry.
_provenance.edition: Jyotirmīmāṃsā of Nīlakaṇṭha Somayājī, ed. K. V. Sarma, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, Hoshiarpur, 1977. Parameśvara's verses are quoted there from his Siddhāntadīpikā (super-commentary on Govindasvāmin's bhāṣya on the Mahābhāskarīya).
_provenance.transcription: Hand-read from an OCR-level e-text of that edition. Only numbers, verse numbers, page numbers and short mnemonic words are kept here; the e-text itself is not redistributed. Page numbers are the e-text's own page markers.
_provenance.glosses: The 'gloss' fields are this repository's plain reading of the Sanskrit. They are not Sarma's translation. Where the reading is not certain the field says so.
_provenance.ahargana: Civil days elapsed since the Kali epoch (Friday 18 Feb 3102 BCE Julian). The 'julian' and 'vara' fields are NOT stored here; kala-dvara.test.js recomputes them from the ahargaṇa by integer arithmetic.
_provenance.numbers: 'printed_number' is the figure Sarma prints above each verse. 'words' and 'word_values' give the verse's own numeral words (bhūtasaṅkhyā, first word = units) so the test can re-derive the printed number; where the e-text words are damaged or ambiguous 'words' is null and the 'flag' says why.

records.gloss: A solar eclipse was seen at Gokarṇa; it was not seen here on the bank of the Nilā.
A solar eclipse was seen at Gokarṇa; it was not seen at the confluence of the Nilā and the sea. v.71 adds that some imagined a colour change at the side of the disc on the Nilā bank.
An eclipse was clearly seen at Nāvākṣetra. At first contact the shadow-pada reading is 40 here, 25 according to others (observer difference).
The Sun slightly eclipsed, seen at Nilā by the keen-sighted. At contact 15 padas; at release mostly 10 less a half.

records.locus: JM p.33, vv.77-78; worked example pp.35-36
records.gloss: Release seen in the afternoon, the shadow at the beginning of 11 padas; the duration exceeds 9 nāḍikās (reading of v.78 not certain). This is the eclipse Nīlakaṇṭha works through as his example.
At release the Sun was seen at sunset; an interval of a quarter nāḍī is mentioned.
At contact the Sun's padas are 24.

records.flag: The e-text word after 'nāga' reads 'adhi'; it reconciles with the printed number only if read as abdhi (4). Not used as a check.
records.gloss: At release time, 5½ padas of the Sun.

records.flag: Mean-syzygy arithmetic puts the nearest mean full moon 1.83 days from this day, the largest offset of the fifteen. Unresolved: either the transmitted number or the day-origin convention. Carried as data, not repaired.
records.gloss: Lunar eclipse. Pada measures at contact and at release are stated; the numeric reading is not fixed here.
On this day no eclipse of the Moon was seen.

records.flag: The e-text 'rasākṣīpurasa' is damaged; the printed number needs 5 where 'pura' normally means 3. Not used as a check.
records.gloss: The Moon was seen slightly eclipsed in the sky by people.

records.flag: The words are Sarma's restoration from the Siddhāntadīpikā (footnote 34_1); the manuscript is broken here.
records.gloss: Lunar. The maximum phase (vimarda) was seen; see also 85b.

records.flag: The first numeral word is damaged in the e-text. Whether this record is lunar is inferred from 'tadvat' in v.85. Not used as a check.
records.gloss: The maximum phase (vimarda) was seen in the same way.

records.flag: Sarma's footnote 1_4 says this Kali day falls in A.D. 1503. Integer arithmetic gives 2 October 1502 Julian. The footnote is the editor's rounding; carried as data.
records.gloss: At Syānandūrapura (modern Trivandrum) and the neighbouring Dravidian places a central (madhyatamaska) eclipse occurred. At contact the Sun was in the western kapāla and a man's shadow was a little over two padas. Between release and sunset there were only four ghaṭikās. Nīlakaṇṭha says that with the Gītikā (Āryabhaṭa) revolutions the parvānta falls at 8 ghaṭikās, and that after the Sun's remaining lambana this is five nāḍikās; the true nati is then greater than the whole contact measure, so by that computation there would be no eclipse at all.

At this ahargaṇa the shadow reading at contact was 11 padas; the elapsed day-part at release is given as fifteen ghaṭikās plus a fraction (the fraction's wording is not certain). At Harihara and the places around it the obscuration was central. Computed with the Moon and the other bodies from the Gītikā revolutions, even on that day there would be no eclipse here.

common_date.flag: The text defines its common ahargaṇa as 8/7500 of a caturyuga on 1,577,917,500 days, which is 1,683,112, not 1,682,112 (= 8 × 210,389 'dhījagannūpura'). Sarma prints 16,82,112 and glosses it A.D. 1504. Both numbers are kept; the discrepancy is the source's, not ours.

moon.flag: The words 'ghaṭasthasya vi-' are Sarma's restoration from the Siddhāntadīpikā (footnote 34_3).

parameshvara_epoch.roundup: v.90 says a half (minute) in excess was taken in the Sun and Moon values (this reading is unverified against Sarma's translation).
parameshvara_epoch.adopted: v.91: 'for the sake of establishing this, another correction has been adopted by us'. v.92 and p.35: when Parahita planets are used, the earlier stated correction (the Śakābda-saṃskāra) is to be applied first.

sakabda_samskara.locus: JM p.11 (verse quoted from the Parahita system, via Sundararāja on the Vākyakaraṇa)

moon_apogee_node.unit: minutes of arc, subtracted from the longitudes of the Moon, its apogee and its node

planets.signs: Mars, Mercury, Saturn added; Jupiter and Venus subtracted; the Sun excepted
planets.flag: Order of the five multipliers is as decoded in the e-text; the pairing to planets is the editor's.

parameshvara_fractions.locus: JM p.35, quoting Siddhāntadīpikā ed. p.322, com. verse 5 as printed
parameshvara_fractions.moon: the Śaka-year minutes diminished by one fifth

ayanamsha.locus: JM p.44, with Sarma's footnote 44_5 (Siddhāntadarpaṇa-vyākhyā p.17)
ayanamsha.gloss: Parameśvara determined by observation that in the Kali year 'rasarāmeṣvabdhi' (4536) the precession (ayanacalana) had completed 15 full degrees. Nīlakaṇṭha reduces it by one tenth of the intervening years in minutes (about 0.9′ a year).

doctrine.sanskrit: तस्मात् शिष्य-प्रशिष्य-परम्परया सर्वैर् अपि परीक्षणं कार्यम्
doctrine.gloss: Therefore testing must be done by everyone, through the succession of disciples and grand-disciples.

doctrine.sanskrit: तस्मात् शिष्याणां ग्रह-गति-परीक्षा-सामर्थ्यापादनम् एव शास्त्र-प्रयोजनम् । ते पुनः दृक्संवादि करणं कृत्वा लोके सञ्चारयेयुः । करणानाम् एव हि व्यावहारिकत्वं सूक्ष्मत्वं च स्यात् ।
doctrine.gloss: The purpose of the śāstra is to give the disciples the ability to test planetary motion. Having made a karaṇa that agrees with observation, they should put it into circulation. Only karaṇas are practical and precise.
